actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

facts.text: The repository is a Unitree GO2 deployment trained with IsaacLab
The repository supports deployment in a MuJoCo simulation and in the real world
Real-world deployment code is still an unchecked TODO item
The simulation entry point uses the 'lo' network interface to build a MujocoWrapper with core/go2/scene_parkour.xml
MujocoEnv loads the MJCF with mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_path and creates the data with mujoco.MjData
MujocoEnv.reset restores the model with mujoco.mj_resetData
MujocoEnv.step writes the action to data.ctrl and advances the model with mujoco.mj_step
The upstream sets model.opt.timestep from the environment configuration's sim.dt
The served scene core/go2/scene.xml includes the robot model go2.xml
The parkour scene core/go2/scene_parkour.xml includes go2.xml and adds a height-field terrain from ../terrain.png
The go2 model compiles angles in radians and looks for meshes in the assets directory
The go2 model option sets an elliptic cone and impratio 100 and states no timestep
The go2 robot body starts at pos -7.5 0 0.5 and carries a free joint
The go2 default class gives every motor a control range of -23.7 to 23.7
The knee default class narrows the motor control range to -45.43 to 45.43
The model declares twelve motor actuators, one for each hip, thigh and calf joint of the four legs
The model declares twelve named hinge joints, three on each leg
The model has a home keyframe with a 19-value qpos and a 12-value ctrl
The model declares joint position, joint velocity, actuator force, IMU orientation, gyro and accelerometer sensors
The flat scene adds a ground plane and a directional light
The parkour terrain is a 200 by 50 height field of size 8.0 2.0 0.3 0.001

determinism.notes: MuJoCo integrates the MJCF deterministically from the reset state and the served model has no random element, so one ctrl sequence and tick count repeat a trajectory; the bridge takes no seed input and a reset restores the model defaults, so no seed selects a different one.  The package's fake backend is deterministic too, but its placeholder motion is not the engine's physics and it offers no snapshot state.

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it parses core/go2/scene.xml with its go2.xml include, takes the twelve actuator control ranges, the joint dimensions and the option time step from the tree, then turns each ctrl into a placeholder joint velocity; it computes no inertia, torque, contact, friction, actuator, sensor or noise dynamics, so no trajectory here is a MuJoCo result
the stand-in loads no mesh or texture and resolves no contact: the scene's floor and the Go2's collision geoms are not simulated physically, and the robot cannot stand or walk in the fake
the model states no option timestep (core/go2/go2.xml:4); the stand-in uses a placeholder library default and the bridge publishes that stand-in value
the stand-in does not apply the model's gear, gain, bias, damping, friction, armature, joint range or force limits, and it treats a motor actuator as a direct joint velocity target
MuJoCo itself was not importable where the gate ran, so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine

the served model is the card's models[0], core/go2/scene.xml; the upstream sim2sim entry point loads core/go2/scene_parkour.xml (core/deployment_player.py:21-22) with the height-field terrain, which this package does not serve

the upstream policy, observation history, joystick command and camera, depth and contact sensors (mujoco_deploy/mujoco_wrapper.py:28-40, core/deployment_player.py:24-28) are not part of this driver, which exposes only the bridge's time, qpos, qvel and ctrl state
snapshot and restore are not offered by the stand-in (it has no mj_getState or mj_setState); the bridge's derived fidelity field still reports the real engine's snapshot support
no physical GO2 is modelled and nothing was validated against the hardware

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.
measures.name: native_checkpoint

safe_state.description: the simulation is held: after an e-stop the runtime refuses every step and reset until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch, and the model data stays readable
